Wooden furniture lasts for generations when it receives a little regular attention. The most common causes of damage are sunlight, dry air and standing moisture, and all three are easy to reduce.
Dust the surface weekly with a soft cloth. Avoid sprays that leave a greasy film, because the film collects more dust and makes the next cleaning harder. For a deeper clean, wipe with a cloth that is barely damp and dry the wood straight away.
Place a coaster under every cup and a mat under every hot dish. Rings and pale marks form quickly, and removing them later usually means sanding and refinishing the whole top.
Once or twice a year, apply a thin coat of paste wax with a cloth, let it stand for fifteen minutes, then buff it in small circles. Work along the grain and keep the layer thin; too much wax looks cloudy.
Keep furniture away from radiators and sunny windows. If that is not possible, rotate the pieces now and then so that the colour fades evenly.
Care of wooden furniture
A short checklist
Dust weekly, wax twice a year, and keep the wood away from heat and damp.
